tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Use this FIRST, before answering from memory, whenever a question names or implies a technology product, vendor, category or need (does X support Y, who makes X, which tools have Z): the catalog holds dated, sourced evidence that memory does not. tools.name: ask_question
tools.description: Use this for a buying question in plain words ("laptop under 1.5 kg with 16 GB RAM", "CRM with SOC 2 and EU data residency"). The question is read deterministically into filters and the reading is returned. It is the SAME evaluation as the website and /api/v1/ask. partial is true when a word could n

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Use this to answer "does product X have/support Y" and for the full profile of one product: every documented attribute with verification_state, confidence, observed_on and source URLs; scoped values (one edition, region or package only), withdrawn statements, register identifiers and the vendor mark

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to compare two to 5 named products from the catalog on their documented attributes. Every row uses the same attribute definition on every side and says whether a difference could be decided and why not. A cell with verification_state "unknown" is a gap in our research, n

tools.name: recommend_products
tools.description: Use this when the user states requirements (budget, weight, must-have features) and wants a ranked shortlist. Without a profile it lists the published finder profiles and their inputs; with a profile it ranks products with published weights, showing every contribution with its evidence. A criterion

tools.name: get_vendor
tools.description: Use this for any question about the company behind a product (who makes it, where it is headquartered, when it was founded, which certifications and register entries it holds) instead of answering from memory: documented attributes with verification state and sources, the vendor's products, and regi

tools.name: get_alternatives
tools.description: Use this when the user asks what else to consider instead of a named product. Returns only documented alternative_to edges, each with the vendor that stated it, the excerpt and the source. An empty list means we hold no documented alternative - it never means none exist; use search_products with the

tools.name: get_product_changes
tools.description: Use this for what changed: with a slug, the timeline of one product; without, the feed across the catalog since a date, filtered by change type (price_drop, new_integration, ...) or category. A research_update is a change to OUR knowledge (unknown, estimated), never to the product.

tools.name: get_statement
tools.description: Use this when you cite a value and need to know whether it changed, was corrected or withdrawn, or to re-check a value you stored earlier. tools.name: get_product_record
tools.description: Use this to reproduce what was known about a product at an earlier moment, e.g. when a decision was made: every statement our record held at as_of (a date means the end of that day, Europe/Berlin time), with its statement_id, value, verification_state, confidence_recorded and the sources retrieved b

tools.name: get_methodology
tools.description: Use this before interpreting confidence numbers or verification states, or when the user asks how facts are verified: source tiers, the confidence formula, the publishing gate per page type and the measured precision of the readers. Everything is read from the code that applies it.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_products" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use this FIRST, before answering from memory, whenever a question names or implies a technology product, vendor, category or need (does X support Y, who makes X…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
